issues.legal_issue: A power-of-attorney holder may not testify in place of a principal about matters within the principal’s personal knowledge or acts done by the principal.
material_facts: The claimants were required to prove that they had an ownership share by showing their independent income and contribution to the property’s purchase.
The claimants did not testify themselves; the tribunal instead permitted one claimant’s husband, who held a power of attorney, to testify on their behalf.
The power-of-attorney holder did not have personal knowledge of the claimants’ relevant financial matters.
issues.conclusion: The power-of-attorney holder could not testify in place of the claimants about matters within their personal knowledge or acts done by them. He could testify about acts he himself performed under the power of attorney and matters within his own personal knowledge.
issues.legal_principle: Order III Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure permit a power-of-attorney holder to act for a principal but do not authorize the holder to depose in place of the principal about the principal’s personal acts or knowledge. The Court approved Shambhu Dutt Shastri v. State of Rajasthan and Ram Prasad v. Hari Narain, and rejected the contrary view in Humberto Luis v. Floriano Armando Luis. It also referred to Vidhyadhar v. Manikrao, under which a party’s failure to testify and submit to cross-examination may support a presumption that the party’s case is not correct.

predicates.civil_proceeding: The dispute is being decided in a civil proceeding.
predicates.agent_offered_as_principal_witness: A party presents an agent to give evidence in place of that party.
predicates.testimony_concerns_principal_personal_kn: The proposed evidence concerns matters personally known to the principal or acts of the principal, rather than acts performed or matters personally known by the agent.
predicates.agent_cannot_testify_for_principal_on_pe: The agent does not give evidence in place of the principal about matters personally known to the principal or acts done by the principal.

issues.definition: When an agent is offered as a witness in a civil proceeding about matters personal to the principal rather than the agent, the agent cannot testify in place of the principal on those matters.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant who bears the burden of proving an ownership share must establish that share through evidence of their own contribution, and an agent’s testimony cannot replace the claimant’s evidence about personal financial matters.
material_facts: The claimants sought to establish shares in property attached in connection with debt-recovery proceedings and bore the burden of proving their ownership.
The purchase consideration had been paid by a Hindu undivided family, a distinct legal entity.
The claimants did not testify personally about their independent income or contributions; the power-of-attorney holder testified instead and lacked personal knowledge of those matters.
The documentary evidence did not establish that the purchase funds came from the claimants’ independent income, and the material relied on included an alteration to a stated ownership share.
issues.conclusion: The claimants failed to prove that they had contributed to the purchase from independent income or that they were co-owners. The tribunal’s finding that they had a share was set aside, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The burden of proving a claimed ownership share rested on the claimants. They had to establish an independent source of income and a contribution to the purchase from that income; names in a sale indenture alone were not conclusive proof of co-ownership. Under Vidhyadhar v. Manikrao, failure by a party to testify and offer themselves for cross-examination may give rise to a presumption that their case is not correct. Evidence from a power-of-attorney holder could not establish matters within the claimants’ personal knowledge.

predicates.claim_to_share_in_property_to_resist_exe: A claimant asserts an ownership share in property to resist its sale in debt-recovery execution proceedings.
predicates.claimant_bears_burden_to_prove_share: The claimant is responsible for proving the asserted ownership share.
predicates.claimant_did_not_testify_personally: The claimant does not give evidence personally about the matters supporting the claimed share.
predicates.agent_lacked_personal_knowledge: The agent who gives evidence does not have personal knowledge of the claimant’s relevant financial matters or contribution.
predicates.evidence_did_not_establish_claimant_inde: The evidence does not establish that the claimant contributed to the property’s purchase from the claimant’s independent income.
predicates.claimant_fails_to_prove_ownership_share: The claimant does not establish the claimed ownership share.

issues.definition: A claimant who must prove a share to resist execution fails to establish it when the claimant does not testify personally, the agent lacks personal knowledge, and the evidence does not establish the claimant’s independent contribution.
